A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemBuilder and contain 20 complete pages, including Appendices A–I. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures and appendix material.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, action-distribution analyses and human evaluations of retrieval attribution and synthetic QA quality in Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, behavioral analyses and Appendix H human evaluations, with limited numerical corrections.

M1.justification: The four-component memory architecture, SFT initialization, ADRPO rewards and gradient weighting, memory operations and inference procedures remain unchanged, including the appendix prompt templates.

E1.justification: LongMemEval remains the sole training source. Both versions evaluate the same LongMemEval, LoCoMo and PerLTQA tasks, question categories and generalization scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain identical comparator sets, including RAG-Session, RAG-Utterance, Mem0, MIRIX, the externally reported Memory-R1 results and the same construction/answer model variants.

E3.justification: Training splits, sample sizes, model roles, retrieval settings, training budgets and QA evaluation procedures are unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.2 and the appendices. The numerical corrections do not document changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The analysis of how training changes memory-action selection is revised through corrected Semantic Memory ADD proportions in Figure 6. The analytical question is retained; the other ablations, training analyses, case studies and human evaluations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Run/seed disclosures, uncertainty reporting and Appendix H inter-annotator agreement reporting remain unchanged. No statistical estimation procedure or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 changes the trained Qwen3-4B answer model's LoCoMo score from 82.00% to 81.12%, matching Table 2, which already reports 81.12% in v3. Figure 6 changes Semantic Memory ADD proportions from 85.2% to 89.2% for SFT and from 96.7% to 92.7% for RL. These are reporting corrections, not demonstrated performance changes from rerunning experiments. Appendix D.3 still reports 82.00%.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, action-space definitions and reward, weighting and optimization equations (1–12) are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning dense rewards, contribution-aware weighting, lightweight memory construction and out-of-distribution generalization.

C2.justification: The interpretations of training behavior, retrieval-based attribution and generalization are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning closed-source answer models and inaccuracies in synthetic QA.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training time, retrieval configuration, cost breakdowns, prompt templates and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and positioning relative to prompting-based and training-based memory systems are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv version/date stamp changes from v3 dated 18 April 2026 to v4 dated 21 June 2026. Apart from the numerical correction in Section 4.3, prose, terminology and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is redrawn with thinner annotation arrows, adjusted typography and corrected Semantic Memory stacked-bar heights. Its four-panel structure, caption and placement are retained; the remaining figures, tables and document layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves internal numerical consistency: Section 4.3 now matches Table 2, and Figure 6's SFT and RL Semantic Memory proportions sum to 100% rather than 96% and 104%. These are useful but limited corrections. Appendix D.3 still gives the inconsistent 82.00% score, while the method, experimental coverage and central conclusions remain unchanged.
